output:
**What I found:** The gate is not doing its job. The auth-internals rule is overwritten: the second block in `eslint.config.mjs` (lines 15–26) sets `no-restricted-syntax` again for `**/*.js`. ESLint flat config replaces the earlier rule's options instead of combining them, so every file is checked only for `debugger`. Lint has stayed green because the auth rule has never run on any file. The fix is to turn it back on and add a test that proves it fails (the record calls this RESTORE).

**Why it matters:** Every green lint run so far says nothing about auth boundaries, and `src/billing/invoice.js` shows other code already depends on auth internals. Turning the rule back on will make `npm run lint` fail on `invoice.js`, and maybe other files. That change has to deal with every violation it uncovers, or merges stop.

**Do this first:**
1. In `eslint.config.mjs`, replace the second block's `no-restricted-syntax` / `DebuggerStatement` entry with `'no-debugger': 'error'`. The two rules then stop sharing a name, so neither can overwrite the other.
2. In the same PR, fix `src/billing/invoice.js:1`: export an invoice-token function from `src/auth/index.js` and import it from there. If other files fail too, list each one by name in a baseline that can only shrink, with an owner. Don't just add them to an ignore list.
3. Add a lint test to CI that checks a known-bad import, for example: `new ESLint().lintText("import { signToken } from '../auth/internal/token.js';", { filePath: 'src/billing/__control__.js' })`. It must report the "Import auth through src/auth/index.js" message, and a `debugger` line must still be flagged. This proves the rule works in the config as actually assembled, not just on its own.

**What I did not check:**
- I couldn't run commands here, so I haven't confirmed which rules ESLint actually applies. `npx eslint --print-config src/billing/invoice.js` shows that.
- I don't know how many other files import auth internals. `npx eslint .` after step 1 gives the count.
- I found no CI config in the repo, so I couldn't confirm where `npm run lint` blocks merge.

```text
Gate:         eslint no-restricted-syntax "auth.internal" import ban, eslint.config.mjs:1-14, run by `npm run lint` (blocks merge)
Stage:        pre-merge static analysis
Trigger:      narrowed — passed while a known-bad input (src/billing/invoice.js:1) existed
Proof:        UNPROVEN — no negative control; no recorded red run
Scope:        declared src/**/*.js minus src/auth/** / effective none (the **/*.js block at lines 15-26 replaces the rule's options everywhere) / delta all auth-internal import checks
Baseline:     none
Status:       BLOCKING (blocks on debugger statements only)
Decision:     RESTORE
Guard:        a CI negative control that lints a src/billing file importing auth/internal through the assembled config and asserts the rule's message; a second control asserts debugger is still flagged
Handoff:      architecture-as-code (the boundary belongs in a per-subsystem architecture config / boundaries rule, not a syntax selector); gate-lifecycle §5 if restoring exposes more violations than one PR can fix
Next action:  switch the debugger check to the core no-debugger rule, fix invoice.js to go through src/auth/index.js, and add the negative control in the same PR
Verification: Not run — no shell available this session; close with `npx eslint --print-config src/billing/invoice.js` and `npx eslint .` (expect red on invoice.js:1 before the fix)
```
